dedupe_keys.name: above us only stars gnss spoofing in russia crimea and syria detected from ship ais and iss gps data c4ads 2019

description: This 66-page report by C4ADS, a nonprofit for data-driven analysis of conflict and security, presents a year-long investigation ending in November 2018 of GNSS spoofing, the transmission of false satellite navigation signals. Using ship positions from the Automatic Identification System (AIS) collected at scale, it found 9,883 suspected spoofing instances in ten or more locations in Russia, Crimea and Syria that affected 1,311 civilian vessels from February 2016, detected where vessels at sea reported positions at nearby airports. It links spoofing to movements of the Russian head of state, to protection of strategic facilities on the Black Sea coast, and, with GPS recordings from a receiver on the International Space Station analysed with the University of Texas at Austin, to a transmitter at Khmeimim airbase in Syria that threatens civil aviation. It also lists what spoofing can do across sectors, such as cellular networks, timing for finance and law enforcement equipment. Coverage: Russia, Crimea, the Black Sea and Syria, 2016 to 2018. Format and access: a free PDF report. Caveats: an investigative report, not peer reviewed; the event data are not published; attributions rely on open-source inference. Simulation uses: real patterns of spoofing extent and duration for hazard exposure and resilience scenarios of ships, aircraft and timing users. Related records: data-gpsjam-gnss-interference maps interference from aircraft data; data-gnss-anomalies-political-violence-2023 links GNSS anomalies to conflict; data-texbat-texas-spoofing-test-battery gives recorded spoofing signals.
